nodes.name: NiO/NiS2 wet-chemical sulfidation on CFP
nodes.procedure: Controlled wet-chemical sulfidation approach to grow NiO/NiS2 heterostructure on carbon fiber paper (CFP), forming ohmic contact. Crystal structure verified by XRD showing cubic NiO and cubic NiS2.
nodes.source_text: Offering a better platform to study the effect of Fe doping, we took advantage of the formation of ohmic contact in NiO / SiS2 grown on carbon fiber paper (CFP) via a controlled wet-chemical sulfidation approach. The crystal structure of the heterostructure was verified by X-ray diffraction (XRD) and the analysis of the pattern indicated the formation of cubic NiO and cubic NiS2.

nodes.name: In situ Fe doping of NiO/NiS2
nodes.procedure: In situ doping strategy during synthesis to prepare xFe-NiO/NiS2 oxide/sulfide heterostructures (x = 0-29.9 wt% Fe as confirmed by ICP-OES, Table S1). Fe content of 8.7% Fe-NiO/NiS2 used as optimal composition. No obvious XRD peak shifts due to similar ionic radii of Ni2+ and Fe3+.
nodes.source_text: Then, we chose an in situ doping strategy to prepare xFe-NiO/NiS2 oxide/sulfide heterostructures (x = 0 - 29.9%) see Table S1), which were confirmed by inductively coupled plasma optical emission spectrometry (ICP-OES) as illustrated in Scheme S1 (see details in Supporting Information). Because of the similar ionic radius of Ni2+ and Fe3+, there are no obvious shifts in the corresponding XRD patterns.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS mappings show uniform Ni, Fe, O distribution while S concentrates on nanoparticles.
nodes.evidence_snippet: SEM energy-dispersive spectrum (EDS) mappings reveal that Ni, Fe and O are uniformly distributed, on the other hand S preferred to concentrate on nanoparticles (Figure S4).

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni 2p3/2 XPS shows Ni-S (854.3 eV), Ni-O (855.9 eV), Ni-OH (856.9 eV) for NiO/NiS2 shifting to 854.3, 855.7, 857.1 eV for Fe-NiO/NiS2; O 1s shows increased basic oxygen (OH ~531.5 eV); S 2p shows increased S-O bonds; Fe 2p3/2 shows Fe-S (706.5 eV) and Fe-O (712.1 eV).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-resolution Ni2p3/2 spectrum showed a slight difference among the materials. The peaks of Ni-S, Ni-O, and Ni-OH in Figure 2b appear at 854.3, 855.9, and 856.9 eV for pristine NiO / SiS2 and then shifted to 854.3, 855.7, and 857.1 eV for Fe - NiO / SiS2 , respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni K-edge FT-EXAFS: Ni-O ~1.5 Å, Ni-S ~1.9 Å, Ni-M ~2.5 Å; O K-edge shows valence states NiO > NiO/NiS2 > Fe-NiO/NiS2 with increased hydroxy groups at ~535 eV.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Three major peaks were observed in the Fourier transform (FT) Ni K-edge extended X-ray absorption fine structure (EXAFS) spectrum in Figure 2e. The first peak around 1.5Å is attributed to Ni-O coordination, the second peak around 1.9Å could be ascribed to Ni-S coordination, and the third major peak is located around 2.5Å corresponding to Ni-M coordination.

nodes.characterization_summary: FTIR shows increased OH bands and emergence of Fe-O at 550 cm-1 and Ni(OH)2 bands at 474 and 511 cm-1 in Fe-NiO/NiS2.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fourier transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy was conducted to detect the bonding information. As shown in Figure S13, the characteristic bands around 1103 cm-1, 1630 cm-1, and 3437 cm-1 are correlated to atmospheric CO vibration, OH bending and stretching vibrations.

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman shows NiS2 Eg at 272-283 cm-1, Ag at 464-472 cm-1, NiO LO at 525 cm-1; in situ shows γ-NiOOH formation at lower potential and reduced NiS2 corrosion with Fe doping.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Raman spectra of the dry samples show three peaks from 200 to 900 cm-1. The peaks at 272-283 cm-1 and 464-472 cm-1 are attributed to Eg and Ag modes of NiS2 and the bands around 525 cm-1 are associated with the single phonon scattering (LO mode) of NiO.

nodes.evidence_snippet: in situ attenuated total reflection infrared (ATR-IR) spectra recorded at 0.1 V intervals were performed to capture the adsorbed intermediate (Figure 4c and Figure 4f).

nodes.evidence_snippet: Wettability measurements in Figure 1i and Figure S9 display that the contact angle (CA) of NiO / SiS2 is 96.89° decreased compared with NiO and NiS2 ... Fe-NiO/NiS displays a CA of 16.53°.

nodes.characterization_summary: UPS shows secondary electron cutoff for work function and valence band structure of NiO.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Ultraviolet photoelectron spectroscopy (UPS) and ultraviolet-visible (UV/Vis) diffuse reflectance absorption spectra were conducted to study the energy levels and the charge-transfer ability of NiO / SiS2 .

nodes.characterization_summary: Pure NiO shows absorption at 350 nm with band gap of 3.57 eV; NiS2 shows no obvious absorption edge indicating metallic character.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Pure NiO showed an absorption at 350 nm with a band gap of 3.57 eV and NiS2 did not show an obvious absorption edge in the UV/Vis region revealing that it has metallic character (Figure S2a, b).
